changes: Removed 'hasta' as nakṣatra: at a Vaiśākha full moon the moon stands near Viśākhā/Anurādhā, so Hasta (two asterisms before Citrā) is astronomically impossible here. 'vudha' is taken as Budhavāra, and 'hasta likhiti' is read as hastalikhita ('written by hand').
Purpose reworded as a devotional dedication.
Notes expanded with the Vudha-as-scribe alternative.

date.as_written: samvat 784 vaiśākhaśuklaḥ paurṇṇamāsī vudhahasta likhiti saṃpūrṇṇadina

notes: The catalogue gives the scribe as 'Vudhahasta ?'. The most likely reading of 'vudhahasta likhiti saṃpūrṇṇadina' is budha(vāra), hasta-likhita, saṃpūrṇa-dina: 'Wednesday, the day the handwritten copy was completed'. Hasta as nakṣatra is ruled out because a Vaiśākha pūrṇimā cannot fall in Hasta. A less likely reading is 'written by the hand of Vudha/Budha', which would make Budha the scribe; because of that doubt no scribe is recorded. The era is not named but is assumed to be NS (the script is Newari): 784 + 880 = c. 1664 CE (April/May). The weekday has not been checked against the calendar. Bhavānī-Śaṅkara is a deity and is not recorded as a person.
